summary: Intermittent user affinity violation during weighted rollout causing split-session responses
description: Issue summary: During a weighted canary rollout for rw-instruct-13b-v2, a subset of user sessions were routed inconsistently between the pinned model and the canary variant. Impact: Customer reports varying completions for the same conversational session across 5-12% of requests originating from the same user/session ID over a 90-minute window. Environment: Dedicated tenant = NimbusDocs, prod us-east, rollout controller v1.5.2, traffic-mapper v0.9.1. Expected: Session affinity (model pin) should persist for the session duration when pinned or when session-level pin exists. Observed: Intermittent affinity loss correlated with rapid weight adjustments and scale events on the canary pool.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant config: pin active -> rw-instruct-13b-v2 pinned for user sessions using session_id cookie. 2) Initiate weighted rollout (canary weight ramp 0->20% over 10m) managed by rollout-controller. 3) Generate steady stream of requests from 30 distinct session_ids at ~2 req/s each. 4) Introduce a scale-up event in the canary pool (add 2 GPUs) around minute 6. 5) Observe routing decisions and model responses in traces and access logs.
observed_behavior: Requests from identical session_id are split between pinned model and canary variant. Split distribution spikes near weight-change windows and immediately after canary pod scale events. Customer reports content drift in 5-12% of sessions (mixed responses).
expected_behavior: A session-level pin should route all traffic for that session to the pinned model for the session lifetime; weight changes should not evict or reseat session affinity until explicit TTL or pin removal.
logs: Proxy traces show routing decisions: trace IDs: 1a3f... saw route decision: 'pinned->rw-instruct-13b-v2' then later 'fallback->rw-chat-7b-quant' for same session key. Rollout-controller logs: 'weight update applied: 12% -> 16%' at 2026-03-10T15:06:32Z. Traffic-mapper debug: 'session-key not found in prefix cache, performing bucket lookup' correlated with scale add event times.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Traffic-mapper cache eviction logic is too aggressive during weight changes and node churn, causing temporary bucket re-evaluation that ignores session pin metadata. Hypothesis B: Rollout-controller updates reach the routing plane out-of-order, briefly replacing pin metadata with weight-only routing rules. Early findings: - Reproduced in staging by simulating scale events and weight ramps; affinitized sessions were re-bucketed. - Traffic-mapper v0.9.1 uses an in-memory LRU keyed by prefix+session_hash with TTL=30s; during heavy weight churn the code path falls back to stateless bucket lookup which doesn't consult session_pin table. - Routing audit traces show 'session_pin' lookup disabled path taken ~8% of the time during weight updates.
temporary_workaround: 1) Pause automated weight ramp for affected tenant and hold canary weight at 0% until hotfix deploy. 2) Add a transient rule in rollout-controller to force session_pin lookup precedence over bucket calculation for active pins. 3) Ask customer to enable the 'strict-session-affinity' flag in tenant config (server-side toggle) to mitigate impact.

Follow-ups: add convergence tests for weight-change + scale events, increase session_pin cache TTL for dedicated tenants, and add observability spike alerts for routing path flips.
